Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Left knee pain; 7 years of left inner knee pain, no injury or trauma 
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 14 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
Normal MRI of the left knee.

Na seriji MR presjeka desnog koljena nalazi se uredna morfologija i intenziteti signala
kolateralnih ligamenata, stražnjeg križnog ligamenta, iliotibijalnog traktusa, patelarnog
ligamenta i tetive m. kvadricepsa.
Linearno intrasupstancijsko povišenje intenziteta signala prednjeg križnog ligamenta pri hvatištu
za tibiju - moguće parcijalna ruptura.
Kalcifikat LCL pri femoralnom hvatištu dimenzija 8 x 5 mm.
Medijalni i lateralni menisk uredne su morfologije i intenziteta signala.
Dublja fissura medijalne fasete patele (hondromalacija III. stupnja).
Manji areal koštanog edema centralnog dijela patele.
Heterogen je intenzitet signala lateralne fasete patele (hondromalacija I. stupnja).
Reducirana je debljina artikulacijske hrskavice medijale i lateralne trohleje femura.
Heterogen intenzitet signala uz vidljive pliće fissure lateralnog platoa tibije te kondila femura
(hondromalacija II./III. stupnja).
Manji izljev u koljenu. Bakerova cista dimenzija 19x29x28mm (APxLLxCC).
Ostale prikazane koštane, mekotkivne i neurovaskularne strukture uredne su morfologije i
intenziteta signala.

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Artrosis
Hallazgos:
Transformación quística difusa del LCA, sin criterios categóricos de rotura. LCP y ligamentos colaterales
dentro de límites normales.
Extensa rotura compleja degenerativa con componente radial total del cuerno posterior, cuerpo y parte del
cuerno anterior del menisco lateral con remanente extruido.
Rotura compleja con componente principal horizontal oblicuo del cuerpo, cuerno posterior y parte de la raíz
meniscal posterior del menisco medial con leve extrusión meniscal.
Úlceras condrales de espesor total de la zona de carga del compartimento femorotibial lateral con cambios
óseos secundarios y proliferaciones óseas periféricas. Úlceras condrales de espesor parcial de distribución
difusa del compartimento femorotibial medial.
Úlceras condrales de espesor parcial y total de la articulación patelofemoral con cambios óseos secundarios
y proliferaciones óseas periféricas.
Leve a moderado derrame articular con sinovitis difusa.
Cambios entesopáticos cuadricipitales distales. Leve aumento de señal del tercio proximal del tendón
rotuliano, sin signos de rotura. Tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de
límites normales.
Impresión:
Transformación quística difusa del LCA, sin criterios de rotura.
Extensa rotura compleja degenerativa del menisco lateral con extrusión asociada.
Rotura del menisco medial, con leve extrusión meniscal.
Avanzados cambios degenerativos del compartimento femorotibial lateral. Condropatía con lesiones grado 2
del compartimento femorotibial medial. Condropatía lesiones grado 3 y 4 de la articulación patelofemoral.
Leve derrame articular con sinovitis difusa.
Cambios entesopáticos cuadricipitales distales. Tendinosis rotuliana proximal

Findings:  There is a moderately large knee effusion. Normal appearances of the medial meniscus. There is a thickened and edematous discoid lateral meniscus with possible degeneration but no definite tear.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  Mild thinning of the medial compartment and patellofemoral articular cartilage is noted but no underlying bony change. Normal lateral compartment articular cartilage.  
Conclusion: Moderate knee effusion. Thickened, edematous and mildly degenerate discoid lateral meniscus noted.

In the medial compartment, the meniscus is not torn and there is no focal chondrosis or chondral injury. 
 The lateral compartment, there is complex tear (main horizontal and vertical components) at the body and posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. There is bone bruise at the posterolateral tibial plateau.  
 The patellofemoral joint appears congruent. There is no cartilage injury. The medial patellofemoral ligament is intact.  
 There is complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament, at mid substance. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact. There is no tibial translation. 
 There is grade II ligamentous sprain (partial tear) of the medial collateral ligament, at mid substance (deep and superficial fibers). There is partial tear of the posteromedial oblique ligament. There is grade II ligamentous sprain of the lateral collateral ligament, at mid substance. Partial tear of the intra-articular portion, popliteus tendon is present. There are tears of the meniscopopliteal fascicles. The popliteofibular ligament is intact. 
 The extensor mechanism is normal.  
 Some amount of right knee effusion is present. The surrounding musculature is normal.   -- Complex tear (main horizontal and vertical components) at the body and posterior horn of the lateral meniscus.  
 -- Complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament, at mid substance. 
 -- Grade II ligamentous sprain (partial tear) of the medial collateral ligament, at mid substance (deep and superficial fibers).  
 -- Posterolateral corner injury by evidence of  
 --      Grade II ligamentous sprain of the lateral collateral ligament, at mid substance. 
 --     Partial tear of the intra-articular portion, popliteus tendon. 
 --      Tears of the meniscopopliteal fascicles.  
 -- Some amount of right knee effusion.  
 -- Bone bruise at the posterolateral tibial plateau.

FINDINGS: A partial injury of the anterior cruciate ligament is demonstrated - anatomical continuity is best appreciated in the coronal plane. There is in fact no associated anterior tibial translation.  Well-preserved medial and lateral tibiofemoral hyaline articular cartilage surfaces, a subcentimeter focus of grade 3/4 articular cartilage loss is noted at the midline femoral trochlea anteriorly. Well-preserved retropatellar articular cartilage.  There is a significant, incompletely imaged knee joint effusion with nonspecific synovitis, no intra-articular loose bodies are present.  There is a popliteus muscle strain posteriorly, there is however no disruption of the corresponding musculotendinous unit or tendon.  The popliteofibular ligament appears sprained, there is furthermore soft tissue edema like signal change at the position of the arcuate ligament complex, suggestive of a sprain pattern - both limbs of the arcuate ligament can however be appreciated on coronal images (series 301 image 26), implying gross structural continuity.  Both collateral ligaments appear intact, as do the PCL, medial meniscus, patellar tendon, distal iliotibial band and marrow signal characteristics.  A tiny cleft is affecting the free edge of the lateral meniscus, at the junction between the body and anterior horn. Minor non calcific distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis also present. No other finding of note.   
</IMPRESSION/> Partial ACL injury with involvement of the popliteus muscle, popliteofibular and arcuate ligaments posterolaterally. Subcentimeter diameter focus of full-thickness cartilage loss with associated reactive marrow changes noted at the midline femoral trochlea.

MRI  KNEE  -  RIGHT

TECHNIQUE:  Unenhanced multiplanar multisequence MR images of the knee.

CLINICAL INDICATION:  Right knee pain, instability, ?meniscal injury vs ACL pathology as per <[Title]> <[Name]>.

COMPARISON:  [Date].

FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout images were reviewed.

Tiny hairline undersurface tear involving posterior horn lateral meniscus. Medial meniscus is intact. 

ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL are intact.

Trace volume joint effusion.

Scattered areas of high-grade chondrosis with underlying bone edema at the patellofemoral compartment. Full-thickness cartilage loss at the medial tibiofemoral compartment.

No fracture or dislocation.

Extensor mechanism is intact. Quadriceps and patellar tendon are intact.

Popliteal fossa cyst.

Soft tissue edema within the subcutaneous tissue anterior to the patella.

INTERPRETATION:
Tiny hairline undersurface tear of the posterior horn lateral meniscus.

Multiple foci of high-grade chondrosis with underlying bone marrow edema at the patellofemoral compartment as well as full-thickness cartilage loss at the medial tibiofemoral compartment. Findings are compatible with moderate OA.
